headline: Chip-design startup Ricursive Intelligence says AI that designs chips could ease the computing crunch by making chips more efficient.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: a founders' pitch at a major conference, not an independently tested result.
importance_line: It points to a way of easing the AI computing squeeze that could help chip buyers and data-centre builders, but the claims are the founders' own and untested outside.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini, founders of Ricursive Intelligence, told TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 that their startup is building AI that designs chips and learns from each design to improve the next. Goldie said demand for computing could rise at least 10,000-fold in five years and argued for more efficient chips rather than 10,000 times more data centres, pointing to a "donut-shaped" layout found by their earlier AlphaChip system.
